content:
{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Inconsistent hemoglobin threshold for gastric cancer indications",
      "quote": "Hemoglobin ≥ 9 g/dL. NOTE: Patients requiring ongoing transfusions or growth factor support to maintain hemoglobin ≥9 g/dL are not eligible. (> 8 g/dL in Gastric Cancer / Gastroesophageal Cancer Indications)",
      "page": 43,
      "section": "5.1 Inclusion Criteria",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The inclusion criteria list a hemoglobin threshold of ≥9 g/dL but then parenthetically allow >8 g/dL for gastric/gastroesophageal cancer indications. This creates ambiguity about which threshold applies to which patients and may lead to inconsistent enrollment or amendments.",
      "fix": "Clarify the exact hemoglobin threshold for each tumor type and remove the parenthetical inconsistency."
    },
  {
      "title": "Exclusion of HER2 mutant NSCLC conflicts with tumor-agnostic design",
      "quote": "HER2 mutant NSCLC.",
      "page": 47,
      "section": "5.2 Exclusion Criteria",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The study aims to enroll patients with HER2 activating mutations across tumor types, but excludes HER2 mutant NSCLC, which is a major tumor type with such mutations. This narrows the target population and may undermine the tumor-agnostic objective.",
      "fix": "Justify the exclusion or consider including HER2 mutant NSCLC if the study is truly tumor-agnostic."
    },
  {
      "title": "Restrictive requirement for post-progression biopsy in HER2-overexpressing cancers",
      "quote": "Patients with breast, gastroesophageal and gastric cancer harboring selected specific HER2 activating mutations ... will be eligible if HER2 is not overexpressed ... in a tissue biopsy taken after documented disease progression following trastuzumab and/or HER2 targeting treatment.",
      "page": 47,
      "section": "5.2 Exclusion Criteria",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Requiring a post-progression biopsy to confirm loss of HER2 overexpression is burdensome and may not be feasible in all patients, potentially limiting enrollment and causing delays.",
      "fix": "Allow alternative methods (e.g., archival tissue if recent) or provide flexibility in biopsy timing."
    },
  {
      "title": "Missing safety monitoring for ILD beyond baseline",
      "quote": "Has a history of (non-infectious) interstitial lung disease (ILD)/pneumonitis that required steroids, has current ILD/pneumonitis, or where suspected ILD/pneumonitis cannot be ruled out by imaging at screening.",
      "page": 47,
      "section": "5.2 Exclusion Criteria",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The protocol excludes patients with ILD at baseline but does not specify ongoing monitoring for ILD during the study, which is a known adverse event of T-DXd. The schedule of activities may lack regular ILD assessment.",
      "fix": "Add scheduled ILD monitoring (e.g., imaging and respiratory symptom assessment) throughout the study."
    },
  {
      "title": "QTcF threshold inconsistent with common oncology practice",
      "quote": "Corrected QT interval by Fridericia's formula (QTcF) prolongation to > 470 msec (females) or > 450 msec (males) based on average of the screening triplicate 12-lead ECG.",
      "page": 47,
      "section": "5.2 Exclusion Criteria",
      "category": "advisory",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The QTcF exclusion thresholds are more stringent than typical oncology trials (often >480 ms), which may exclude patients who could safely participate and increase screen failures.",
      "fix": "Consider aligning thresholds with standard oncology guidance (e.g., >480 ms) unless justified by drug risk."
    },
  {
      "title": "Ambiguous washout for immunotherapy",
      "quote": "Anti-cancer chemotherapy (Immunotherapy [non-antibody-based therapy]), retinoid therapy, mBC; hormonal therapy: ≥ 3 weeks",
      "page": 43,
      "section": "5.1 Inclusion Criteria",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The phrase 'Immunotherapy [non-antibody-based therapy]' is ambiguous; it is unclear which agents are included and whether the 3-week washout applies to all immunotherapies, potentially leading to protocol deviations.",
      "fix": "Define immunotherapy more precisely and specify washout periods for each class."
    },
  {
      "title": "No upper age limit but other age restrictions may apply",
      "quote": "Male and female patients must be at least 18 years of age at the time of signing the ICF. Other age restrictions may apply as per local regulations.",
      "page": 43,
      "section": "5.1 Inclusion Criteria",
      "category": "advisory",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The phrase 'Other age restrictions may apply as per local regulations' is vague and could lead to inconsistent enrollment across sites.",
      "fix": "Specify any age restrictions or remove the vague statement."
    },
  {
      "title": "Endpoints lack patient-reported outcomes despite mention in abbreviations",
      "quote": "MDASI, MD Anderson Symptom Inventory; SGRQ-I, St George’s Respiratory Questionnaire for patients with Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis",
      "page": 37,
      "section": "3 Objectives and Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The abbreviations list includes MDASI and SGRQ-I, but these patient-reported outcome measures are not listed in the objectives and endpoints table, suggesting they may be missing from the study design.",
      "fix": "Add PRO endpoints to the objectives and endpoints or remove the abbreviations if not used."
    }
  ]
}
